meta.title: Foyer
meta.description: Set rules for your AI assistants so they don’t spend or book without agreement.

home.title: Keep your AI assistants from fighting over your money.
home.lead: One bot books travel. Another watches the budget. They both act in your name, but they want different things. You write the rules. Foyer checks each request against those rules before anything is paid or booked.

outline.constitutionLead: You write what is allowed. Every assistant follows the same text. The court reads it too.
outline.gatewayLead: An assistant cannot pay, book, or message the outside world on its own. It asks through Foyer. If nobody objects, it goes through.
outline.courtLead: If they disagree, the court decides: go ahead, block it, find a middle, or ask you. If it cannot decide, you decide. You can appeal.

replay.title: How a request is decided
replay.lead: A request, an objection if someone objects, then one of four outcomes.

c.asked: Send the client spreadsheet with emails

d.asked: Promise the client delivery next Friday
d.counter: Reply without a hard delivery date
d.decided: Reply without a hard delivery date

check.title: How to test
check.lead: Walk this list on the public URL. The product is the cabinet, not the harness.
items: A person without OpenAPI can connect an assistant in a few copy-pastes.
With one own assistant, a dispute still appears (test guardian; canned phrases only).
The dispute goes through agent calls, not “I am budget” clicks.
All four outcomes show up, including allow_b as a counter and as a pure block.
A remedy verdict names remedy_action; after a pass the assistant acts, without a human reading prose.
An untouched request still resolves when nobody pokes the app (the tick).
After a pass the test client acts (or the test sees it). Appeal still exists.
A live cabinet can show an on-chain tx when consensus lands.
The harness does not pass itself off as the product.
The public URL keeps state after a reload.
Someone else’s cabinet stays invisible without its agent key or the owner’s wallet.

connectDoc.title: Connect your runtime
connectDoc.lead: Your assistant talks to Foyer with an agent key. Paste the MCP block from the cabinet. Spawn is a harness, not this path.
connectDoc.product: This is the product path: Cursor, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, or OpenClaw. A real guardian is a second assistant you connect the same way. Wizard test clients only match canned phrases.
connectDoc.off: Any action into the world starts as a request here. After a pass the assistant does it with its own tools and reports.
connectDoc.prompt: Put the three cabinet lines in the system prompt. The lock is still the tools, not the prompt.
connectDoc.cursor: Cursor → Settings → MCP. Paste the block. Restart the agent if it was already open.
connectDoc.claude: Paste the same block into Claude Desktop MCP settings.
connectDoc.chatgpt: Add an HTTP MCP server. URL and bearer header are in the block.
connectDoc.openclaw: Paste the same block into OpenClaw MCP settings.
connectDoc.http: Writing your own client? Use the HTTP / OpenAPI tab in the cabinet. Same key. GET /api/openapi.
connectDoc.spawn: No runtime at all? The landing demo is one shared cabinet you can look at. That is not your house.

legal.title: Legal notice
legal.lead: Foyer is a public test. This is not a company filing and not legal advice.
legal.body: The service is offered as-is while we try the protocol. Do not put real money or production agents on it yet.
legal.contact: Questions: leave an email on the home page.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: We keep as little as we can.
privacy.body: Wallet address if you sign in. Email if you join the waitlist. Hashed IP on public writes, for rate limits, without request bodies. Agent keys stay in your runtime.
